instructions.task: Read the Craigslist listing and the buyer-seller negotiation chat. How does the negotiation end? Pick the option that best describes the end of the chat.
notes: Focus on the last price offered and how the other side responded to it.

Acceptance is often terse or implicit: 'ok', 'fine', 'yes', 'fair enough', 'sounds good', 'done', 'deal', 'I'm on my way', or going straight to arranging pickup, delivery, a meeting, a test drive, payment or paperwork for that price.
A garbled or odd final line (typos, a joke) does not undo an acceptance that already happened.

examples.chat_end: Seller: I can give you $75 last price. Buyer: I can do 70. Seller: Okay then you still will have to come pick it up yourself. Buyer: ok
Buyer: meet halfway, bring it down $15? Seller: Yeah I do that put in your offer.
Seller: I think 1300 will work since I need to get it sold. Buyer: Oh, sorry for being rude
Buyer: Ok, that sounds fair. Seller: great, when do you want to come check it out in person? Buyer: Yes I will have cash in hand
Buyer: $10000 and you bring it to me. Seller: 10000 and you will come get it yourself
Buyer: ok how about 2900. Seller: Well if you can go 2950 it would save me the trouble of holding the open house.
Buyer: can it be delivered? if not, the most im willing to pay is $70 if i have to go pick it up. Seller: Yes we will gladly deliver it for you, no problem!
Seller: Yeah I am selling it for 75$ are you interested? Buyer: Yes. It looks great. Did you alter the device or trust the person who did?

examples.whole_chat: Buyer: I seen you are asking $55. Would you go lower if I come pick it up tonight? Seller: Yes, I'll go 5 lower

criteria.explicit_accept: A specific price stated in the chat was explicitly accepted by the other side ('deal', 'ok $110', 'that works', 'sounds good').
criteria.implicit_accept: A specific price stated in the chat was accepted implicitly or tersely: the other side said 'fair enough'/'ok'/'yes', agreed to a condition attached to it (pickup, delivery, extras), or moved on to arranging pickup, a meeting, a test drive, payment or paperwork. Small open details (utilities to be worked out later) are fine.
criteria.closing_offer_pending: After a real back-and-forth, the chat ends on one side's final offer (e.g. 'make that $6,600 and you have a deal', 'I'll send the offer at $1900', 'can I give you $6 for both?') that was not rejected, with the two sides close together or one side already giving in.
criteria.still_apart: The chat ends with the two sides still disagreeing on price, or a counteroffer with new terms (e.g. an added deposit) that the other side never answered.
criteria.rejected_or_walked_away: One side rejected the final offer, said they were too far apart, or walked away.
criteria.price_never_settled: One side said 'ok'/'sounds good'/'fine' but not to a settled stated price: the price was never named in the chat ('see final offer directly'), only a side question (delivery, pets) was answered, or after an apparent agreement a side disputes the price again ('the offer says $2695 but I can only afford $2200') and the chat ends there.
criteria.no_negotiation: Hardly any conversation: the chat is empty or has only one or two messages with no back-and-forth, even if one message states a price or says 'Agree'/'Cool' (e.g. only the seller's opening line 'I will let it go for $260', or 'I would like to buy your house' / 'Cool'). No real exchange of offers took place.
